text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service \"inference-prod-api\" — Incident ID: PD-20260315-4512. Priority: P1. Trigger: increased 5xx rate (75% over baseline) from edge-gateway clusters. Paging: default fallback route applied.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty note: Page routed to schedule 'default-ops' -> escalations to 'oncall-all'. See https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-20260315-4512

alice_m: whoa lots of pings. I'm getting pages from multiple teams. Is this the right service?

bob_s: I think PD routing updated earlier today by infra-automation? cc @ops-liaison

ops-liaison: yep that change rolled at 08:12 UTC — a migration script intended to map unknown services to 'infra-fallback' but the rule name was mistyped and matched the wrong tag (tag:service:inference -> tag:service:*). rolling back now.

charlie_oncall: ack. I'm on call for inference-prod but didn't get the original manual page, only the fanout. Confirming impact: customer latency spikes for request batches hitting kv-cache miss.

alice_m: customers in EU reported 502s. SLOs alerted. Does runbook say to scale replicas or check routing?

sre-manager: runbook link: https://console.redwood.ai/runbooks/inference-5xx — step 1: check model pool health, step 2: check routing fallback. Looks like fallback policy sent to 'oncall-all' which caused all teams to be noisy.

bob_s: snippet of the PD rule that caused it (from the migration commit):
```
- match: service_tag: "tag:service:*"
  action: route_to: schedule: "oncall-all"
  fallback: true
```
That *should* have been `tag:service:unknown`. human typo.

ops-liaison: rollback in progress — disabling the faulty rule (PD API):
```
curl -X DELETE \ 
  "https://api.pagerduty.com/rules/PR-3892" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Token token=$PD_TOKEN" 
```
Will patch infra-config repo right after.

charlie_oncall: I can start a quick mitigation: temporarily scale inference-servant replicas + isolate edge region to reduce cross-region fanout. Running `kubectl -n inference scale deploy/servant --replicas=6`.

alice_m: :thumbsup: apply scaling. I can also flip proxy routing to prefer local pools (config patch below):
```
PATCH /v1/proxy/config HTTP/1.1
{ "route_preference": ["local-pool","regional-pool","fallback"] }
```

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-20260315-4512 acknowledged by charlie_oncall at 2026-03-15T08:15:30Z

bob_s: monitoring: error-rate trending down post-scale, kv-cache hit ratio improving. Hoping rollback + scale gives breathing room.

sre-manager: quick postmortem notes while fresh: 1) migration script lacked unit test for pattern matching; 2) default fallback name collision risk; 3) add invariant check in deploy pipeline to prevent wildcard tag matches.

ops-liaison: file PR created to add protection and a canary flag for routing-rule rollouts: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/pd-routing/compare/fix-wildcard-guard

alice_m: can we confirm no customer data exposure? This was routing only — no config drift to data plane. I'll run through compliance checklist.

charlie_oncall: customers still seeing intermittent 502s in EU but much reduced. I'll keep oncall until stable, then handoff to bob_s for follow-up tomorrow. Tentative handoff at 09:30 UTC.

sre-manager: thanks team. After the incident we should schedule a short blameless review. Also add an automated test that rejects PD rules with `*` service tags unless explicitly flagged.

ops-liaison: rollback completed at 2026-03-15T08:20:45Z. Closing noisy pages.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-20260315-4512 status: mitigated (notes updated).

alice_m: :eyes: filing customer impact summary to #support-ops and will draft external comms if needed.

charlie_oncall: handing off to bob_s now. bob_s, you have the rest.

bob_s: taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours then add remediation action items. Thanks all. :heart:
